relationships.subject: SR144528
relationships.evidence_quote: the CB2 antagonist SR144528 (1 mg/kg, i.p., daily) inhibited the anti-allodynic effect of BCP (100 mg/kg, gavage, 1×/day) in the von Frey experiments

relationships.subject: GW405833
relationships.evidence_quote: the selective CB2 agonist GW405833 (1 mg/kg, i.p., daily) reversed OXA-induced mechanical allodynia

relationships.subject: β-caryophyllene
relationships.evidence_quote: BCP prevented mechanical and cold allodynia when administered at the onset of OXA therapy, as well as reversed an established OIPN phenotype in the therapeutic protocol

relationships.subject: oxaliplatin
relationships.evidence_quote: OXA-treated mice showed an increased level of TNF, IL-1β, and IL-6, and decreased content of the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10

relationships.subject: β-caryophyllene
relationships.evidence_quote: These anti-inflammatory effects exerted by BCP accompany decreased ROS production in the spinal cord when compared to OXA-treated mice

relationships.subject: β-caryophyllene
relationships.evidence_quote: GW9662 caused a transient blockage of the BCP anti-allodynic response at the dose tested

key_findings: BCP, a CB2 agonist, prevented and reversed oxaliplatin-induced mechanical and cold allodynia; CB2 antagonist blocked mechanical but not cold effects.
BCP reduced spinal cord cytokines, ROS and lipid peroxidation without impairing oxaliplatin antitumor activity.
